stages.title: Citizen arrives
stages.what: The front door. One page serves two audiences — a citizen reporting a problem, and an officer signing in to work on one.

stages.title: Registration
stages.what: A multi-step account setup: identity, contact, security, photo. Nothing is saved until the citizen confirms what was read.

stages.title: CNIC verification
stages.what: The camera watches the live frame, captures when the card is steady, then the model is asked whether the photograph is genuinely readable — field by field — before anything is extracted.

stages.title: Authentication
stages.what: Better Auth issues an httpOnly session cookie. Where somebody lands afterwards is decided by what their account IS, never by which button they pressed.

stages.title: Report a problem
stages.what: Photograph, describe by voice or text, confirm the location. Camera-first, because a photograph is the one thing every citizen can produce.

stages.title: AI processing
stages.what: Vision identifies what the photograph shows; speech turns a spoken description into text. Both feed the routing decision.

stages.title: Routing & grouping
stages.what: One agent picks the department that owns the problem; another decides whether this is a NEW problem or another voice on one already reported. This is why 108 reports become 16 issues.

stages.title: Civic issue
stages.what: The unit of government work. Many citizen reports link to one issue, so a department sees one job rather than a queue of the same complaint.

stages.title: Authority workspace
stages.what: The department's operations view: the queue, the case file, the AI's reasoning, and the evidence behind every grouped report.

stages.title: Discussion
stages.what: Issue-scoped chat with @mentions. Flat by design: any member may open a thread and pull in any colleague, so coordinating never means leaving for WhatsApp.

stages.title: Status
stages.what: Reported → In process → Resolved, computed from the department's OWN workflow stages rather than a fixed enum, so each department defines what finished means.

stages.title: Resolved & published
stages.what: The citizen sees the outcome, and every authority's resolution rate is published against the workload it actually carries.

src/components/civic/resolution-donut.ts.summary: A donut showing how a caseload is split across the three stages. Inline SVG rather than a charting library: three arcs need no dependency, and a chart that renders on the server has no loading state to design around. Colours are the same red/amber/green used everywhere else, so the chart needs no legend to be understood — though it has one anyway.

src/lib/civic/format-date.ts.summary: The ONE way a timestamp is turned into text anywhere in CivicAI. `date.toLocaleString()` with no arguments reads the RUNTIME's default locale and timezone. src/lib/civic/next-path.ts.summary: Validating a `?next=` redirect destination. Kept free of `server-only` so the rule can be unit-tested directly: this decides where somebody lands the instant after they type their password, which is exactly when they are least likely to check the address bar.

A citizen photographs the front, is asked for the back, and photographs the front again — easily done, the card is in their hand and both sides look like "the card". src/lib/cnic.ts.summary: Pakistani CNIC helpers — format only. IMPORTANT: nothing in this file establishes that a CNIC is genuine. It checks that a number is *shaped* like a CNIC. Any user-facing wording must say "format checked", never "verified". Real verification requires an authorised NADRA integration, which CivicAI does not have.

src/lib/gov/format.ts.summary: Display formatting for the government portal. Pure functions with no React and no server imports, so they are unit-tested directly (tests/gov-format.test.ts) rather than through a rendered page. Everything is stored UTC and formatted in the viewer's own timezone — an officer in Karachi and one in Islamabad read the same instant correctly without the server guessing which they are.

src/lib/i18n/locales.ts.summary: CivicAI will eventually serve citizens in several Pakistani languages. Stage 1 ships English only, but the locale list and text direction live here from the start so that adding Urdu is a translation job, not a refactor.
